The researchers used e-beam deposition to deposit Ni-based thin films on quartz substrates.
The Ni content was varied from 10at% to 50at%.
Heat treatment was used to improve crystallization and conductivity.
The Sn-40Al-10Ni film showed improved EMI shielding and electrical conductivity.
The EMI shielding measurement was performed using a coaxial holder with a frequency range of 300 kHz to 3 GHz.
The accuracy of the EMI shielding measurement was ±10 ppm.
The thickness range of the Sn-40Al-xNi films was 300 nm to 720 nm.
Increasing Ni content can enhance the growth of nano-grains.
The researchers used XRD to analyze the crystallization of the Ni-based thin films.
The Sn-40Al-10Ni film showed improved EMI shielding at high frequencies.
The researchers used a vacuum furnace to perform annealing experiments.
The Ni-based thin films were deposited on quartz substrates with different orientations.
The researchers used a scanning electron microscope (SEM) to analyze the surface morphology of the Ni-based thin films.
The Sn-40Al-10Ni film showed improved electrical conductivity after annealing.
The researchers used a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) to measure the magnetic properties of the Sn-40Al-10Ni film.
